pdf_explanation: Individual patterns on the left are rotated by 180° about their own position to get the figure on the right.
why: Each of the four small patterns in figure 1 turns upside down (rotates 180°) but stays in its own corner to make figure 2. Do the same to the four patterns in figure 3: the top-left one gets its bracket at the bottom-right, the top-right one gets its bracket at the bottom-left, and so on. Only option 2 shows this. Option 1 looks close, but its bottom-left pattern has the bracket at the bottom-left instead of the top-right.
trick: When a figure has several small parts, check each part one by one in its own place. A 180° turn moves every corner mark to the opposite corner.
note: PDF answer B checked: rotating each pattern of figure 3 by 180° in place gives exactly option B; the other options each differ in at least one pattern.
